author: ojiudezue
title: Lock arrival guard holds only 'stale-source' arrivals; flat hold and dropout rule both rejected on measured data
summary: Oji's phone-app dropouts made HA person fall back to an iPad that had read home for days: 78 sub-second false arrivals in a week, each of which the lock regime counts (not_home->home skips the 15-min check) and 49 of which also crossed the 1,500 m proximity radius. The guard holds an arrival only if the tracker that reports home did not itself change at the edge.
why: Operator bar: never delay a real unlock ('feeling locked out makes URA feel completely unreliable'). Measured arrival->garage-open gap min 1.9 s, so a flat 5 s hold would disable a remote at press ~1 in 27 arrivals. Confusion matrix over 118 edges: flat hold 40/40 real held; dropout-in-last-N-s 1/40 (Ezinne); GPS-source 19/40; stale-source 0/40 real, 78/78 blips, margin 0.0003 s vs >=4119 s. Boot window exempt because HA restart resets tracker timestamps.
alternatives_considered: Flat 5 s hold on every arrival
Hold only after a tracker dropout
implications: Dormant today (no person has two GPS trackers since the 11-11 iPad trim) but closes a lock-release path that one added device reopens. Same blips still open Security's 5-min expected-arrival window (STALE-SOURCE-ARRIVAL-CONSUMERS-1).
revisit_trigger: Any real arrival held (arrival_hold count >0 outside boot window with a source tracker that changed at the edge), or a person gains a second GPS tracker.
